metadata.name: polaris
metadata.description: Polaris — undercollateralized BNPL, subscriptions and payments on Solana

instructions.name: charge_due
docs: Permissionless. The subscription analogue of `collect_installment`.

accounts.name: keeper
docs: Permissionless, and fee-payer only.
Funds can only travel subscriber → merchant on a schedule the subscriber
already agreed to, so a third-party keeper calling this is harmless and
keeps collection decentralised.

instructions.name: collect_installment
docs: Permissionless. Collects exactly the installment that is due.

accounts.name: keeper
docs: Permissionless. The keeper signs only to pay the transaction fee — it
has no authority over the money.
This is where KeeperHub's gas sponsorship goes: on Solana the fee payer
is simply a different signer from the token authority, so a keeper that
holds no stablecoin and touches no borrower balance still gets the
transaction landed.

accounts.name: borrower
docs: The borrower signs their own origination.
On EVM this was `onlyOriginator`: a permissioned backend called
`createLoan(borrower, ...)` against an allowance the borrower had
granted in an earlier transaction. Solana can put the SPL `Approve` and
this instruction in **one atomic transaction**, so the borrower signs
once at checkout and the permissioned-originator role — along with the
window between approving and borrowing — disappears entirely.

accounts.name: borrower_token_account
docs: The account every installment will be drawn from. Pinned into the loan
so a keeper cannot later point collection at a different one.

instructions.name: initialize
docs: `grace_period` and `min_interval_seconds` are fixed here for the life of
the deployment. Zero means the default for either.

accounts.name: treasury
docs: Where protocol fees are swept. Must hold the protocol stablecoin.

accounts.name: liquidity_vault
docs: The pool merchants are paid from and repayments land in.

accounts.name: collateral_vault
docs: Locked borrower collateral. Held apart from lending liquidity so a
withdrawal of idle capital can never reach into it.

instructions.name: liquidate
docs: Permissionless. The condition is checked inside the instruction, so
there is no window between the check and the action.

accounts.name: keeper
docs: Permissionless, and fee-payer only — same as collection.

instructions.name: pay
docs: `order_ref` is the merchant's 32-byte reference for this order. It
addresses the payment account, which is what makes a retried checkout
idempotent without a duplicate check.

accounts.name: payment
docs: Seeded by (merchant, order reference).
On EVM this was `keccak256(merchant, orderId)` used as a mapping key,
with an explicit `if (payments[id].paidAt != 0) revert DuplicatePayment`.
Here the address *is* the guard: a retrying checkout hits an account
that already exists and `init` fails. The check cannot be forgotten,
because it is not a check.
The reference is the identifier itself rather than a digest of a string
carried alongside it. Nothing to recompute means nothing to disagree.

accounts.name: payout
docs: Where this merchant is settled. Must hold the protocol stablecoin.

instructions.name: repay
docs: Borrower-signed. Any amount, including early payoff.

accounts.name: borrower
docs: The borrower's own signature. This path takes an arbitrary amount, so it
is exactly the one that must not be permissionless.

accounts.name: subscription
docs: Seeded by (subscriber, plan). One live subscription per pair is a
property of the address, so a double-subscribe is impossible rather than
merely checked for. `init_if_needed` is what lets a cancelled
subscription be restarted in the same slot; the status guard below is
what stops it being restarted while still active.

types.name: CreditProfile
docs: Per-user credit state.
On EVM this was split across `ScoreManager._profiles`,
`LoanEngine.activeDebtOf` and `CollateralVault.lockedOf` — three contracts
that had to be kept consistent with each other through `setWriter` and
`setSeizer` grants. Inside one program they are one account, so the
consistency problem does not exist.

fields.name: active_debt
docs: Everything this user currently owes across every open plan.

fields.name: seized_collateral
docs: Set when a liquidation seizes collateral, so it cannot be double-seized.

fields.name: installment_index
docs: 0-based, to match `installment_due_at`, so an indexer can join the event
to the schedule without an off-by-one.

fields.name: installments_paid
docs: Installments the money received actually covers, after this payment.

fields.name: merchant
docs: The merchant's registry PDA, not their wallet.

fields.name: borrower_token_account
docs: The token account the borrower is charged from. Pinned at origination so
a keeper cannot be pointed at a different account later.

fields.name: payout
docs: Token account that receives settlement.

fields.name: max_order_value
docs: BNPL exposure is a function of who is selling as much as who is buying.

types.name: Payment
docs: Seeded by (merchant, order id), so a retrying checkout cannot pay twice:
the second `init` fails because the address is already occupied.

fields.name: order_ref
docs: The 32-byte reference this payment settles. Also its PDA seed.

fields.name: merchant
docs: The merchant registry PDA that owns this plan.

types.name: Protocol
docs: Global configuration and the protocol's own ledgers.
This PDA is also the authority on the liquidity and collateral vaults, and
the delegate every borrower approves. One signer for the whole protocol.

fields.name: stablecoin
docs: The stablecoin mint. Every token account the protocol touches must match.

fields.name: treasury
docs: Where protocol fees are swept. A token account, not a wallet.

fields.name: grace_period
docs: How long an installment may be overdue before the loan is liquidatable.
Set at initialization rather than as a constant: a consumer book wants
days, a machine-to-machine book wants minutes, and a devnet deployment
wants seconds so the liquidation path can be demonstrated without
waiting three days.

fields.name: min_interval_seconds
docs: Floor on an installment interval and a subscription period. Fixed at
initialization, like the grace period, so it cannot be lowered under a
schedule that is already running.

fields.name: protocol_fees_accrued
docs: Accrued protocol share of interest, not yet swept.

fields.name: bad_debt
docs: Unrecovered value from liquidations. The protocol's own loss ledger.

fields.name: fee_bps
docs: Fee on direct payments and subscription charges.

fields.name: credit_multiplier_bps
docs: Basis points of credit granted per unit of locked collateral.

types.name: Subscription
docs: Seeded by (subscriber, plan), so one live subscription per pair is a
property of the address rather than a check that can be forgotten.
